requirements.requirement: Establish a persistent integrity baseline for files under /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: A SHA-256 manifest containing 307 /etc files and symlinks was created with root-only state-directory and baseline permissions. An immediate check was clean, and the identical baseline hash, entry count, files, and clean result remained after a confirmed node restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow later changes within /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A bounded test modified an /etc file, and the checker identified its exact path as CHANGED, reported one detected change, and returned the expected nonzero status. Restoring the file returned the system to a clean result. A daily periodic job and running, boot-enabled scheduler provide ongoing reporting.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel while using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Alpine Linux 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts were observed before the work and again after restart. The implemented checker uses tools directly demonstrated on the node, and the unsuccessful AIDE installation did not result in an installed package or platform change.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The baseline is protected, detects and reports a demonstrated change, survives restart, and operates without changing the installed Alpine release or kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered scheduler, baseline data, files, and clean integrity state were all captured.
limitations: The daily scheduler was shown configured, running, and recovered after restart, but an automatically triggered daily execution was not directly observed; manual change detection and reporting were directly tested.
Failed-service lifecycle collection used a systemd-specific probe unsupported on Alpine, although direct OpenRC checks showed crond healthy before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The substantive mutations—installing the checker and protected baseline, adding the daily job, enabling crond, and restarting the node—were directly connected to the task or mandatory restart protocol. The integrity probe was bounded and fully reverted. The failed AIDE installation has no evidence of changing state. One minor unnecessary residue remained: cmd-09126f17d2b1430e redirected reboot output to /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, which was still present after execution and was not cleaned up.
